name: US-session extreme move reversed into the Asia session
rule: Conventions: signal mode on CRYPTO_1H, independent per symbol, all times UTC; time = bar OPEN in epoch seconds; bar k covers [time[k], time[k]+1h) and close[k] is the price at the END of the bar; H(k)=floor(time[k]/3600)%24; D(k)=(floor(time[k]/86400)+4)%7 (0=Sun..6=Sat); a 'bar H=h' is the bar that opens at h:00, so its close is the (h+1):00 price. signal(bars,i,ctx) is evaluated at the close of bar i using only bars 0..i and returns the position (+1/0/-1) held over bar i+1; 'enter/exit' means the returned position changes at bar i. ret1[k]=close[k]/close[k-1]-1; sigma(j) = ctx.rollingStd('ret',720,j) (sample std of the 720 hourly returns ending at bar j; NaN or <=0 means no trade); a z-score of an n-bar move R is R/(sigma(.)*sqrt(n)) with sigma taken at the bar BEFORE the move starts. State lives in ctx.state (initialise with `=== undefined` checks); position, flags and histories are reset only as stated. Long-only specs never return -1; 'long/short' specs may. One position at a time per symbol; while a position is held its entry rules are not re-evaluated unless stated. Params are fixed a priori and are never tuned. Long/short. At bar i with H(i)==20 (close = 21:00): R = close[i]/open[i-6]-1 (the 14:00-21:00 US session, 7 bars i-6..i); z = R/(sigma(i-7)*sqrt(7)). If flat: z<=-2.0 -> position +1; z>=+2.0 -> position -1; otherwise 0. Hold exactly 8 bars (bars H=21,22,23,0,1,2,3,4) and return 0 from the bar whose close is 05:00 onward (i.e. set position 0 at the bar i+8, the bar with H==4).
rationale: Large moves made in the US session are partly inventory and leverage driven; the thinner Asia session has been argued to give part of them back, which is the intraday analogue of liquidity-provision reversal. Testable per symbol with a pre-fixed 2 sigma gate.
source: Campbell, Grossman, Wang (1993) 'Trading volume and serial correlation in stock returns' QJE; Gao-Han-Li-Zhou (2018) intraday momentum JFE; Kaiko 2023 intraday liquidity by session

name: TTM squeeze release on hourly crypto
rule: Conventions: signal mode on CRYPTO_1H, independent per symbol, all times UTC; time = bar OPEN in epoch seconds; bar k covers [time[k], time[k]+1h) and close[k] is the price at the END of the bar; H(k)=floor(time[k]/3600)%24; D(k)=(floor(time[k]/86400)+4)%7 (0=Sun..6=Sat); a 'bar H=h' is the bar that opens at h:00, so its close is the (h+1):00 price. signal(bars,i,ctx) is evaluated at the close of bar i using only bars 0..i and returns the position (+1/0/-1) held over bar i+1; 'enter/exit' means the returned position changes at bar i. ret1[k]=close[k]/close[k-1]-1; sigma(j) = ctx.rollingStd('ret',720,j) (sample std of the 720 hourly returns ending at bar j; NaN or <=0 means no trade); a z-score of an n-bar move R is R/(sigma(.)*sqrt(n)) with sigma taken at the bar BEFORE the move starts. One position at a time per symbol; while a position is held its entry rules are not re-evaluated unless stated. Params are fixed a priori and are never tuned. Long/short. s = ctx.rollingStd('close',20,i); a = ctx.atr(20,i); sqOn = (2.0*s < 1.5*a) (Bollinger band 2 sigma inside the Keltner 1.5 ATR band, both centred on the 20-bar SMA). state.run counts consecutive sqOn bars (reset to 0 when sqOn false). Release at bar i: sqOn false at i AND state.run (value before reset) >= 6. At the release bar, mom = close[i] - ((ctx.donchian(20,i).upper+ctx.donchian(20,i).lower)/2 + ctx.sma('close',20,i))/2; enter +1 if mom>0, -1 if mom<0. Hold until sign(mom) at a later bar is opposite to the position (mom<0 for long / >0 for short) or 48 bars have passed, then 0.
